audits.title: Audit on PRN Prescriptions in Adult Inpatient Female Ward
audits.standard: NICE guidance on PRN prescribing and local Trust policy
audits.setting: Adult acute inpatient female psychiatric ward

cycle1.result: PRN reviewed in last 7 days 25%; oral and IM grouped 7.2%; minimum dose documented 10.7%; maximum 24-hour dose 100%; indication 100%.

audits.intervention: Guidelines added to junior doctor induction, weekly discussion with team pharmacist, prompts on the medication chart and weekly PRN review in ward MDT.

cycle2.result: PRN reviewed in last 7 days 56%; oral and IM grouped 28%; minimum dose 24%; maximum 24-hour dose 100%; indication 96%.

audits.other_findings: Improvements did not reach the 100% standard.
audits.citation: Adhikari A, Shah S, Dhaliwal M, Chalaby A. Audit on PRN Prescriptions in Adult Inpatient Female Ward. BJPsych Open. 2024;10(S1):S211-S211. doi:10.1192/bjo.2024.524.

audits.title: Evaluating PRN Medication Prescribing Practices in Mental Health Services: A Comparative Audit Following a Serious Incident
audits.standard: 13 predefined PRN prescribing standards including generic naming, dose intervals, BNF limits and regular reviews
audits.setting: Inpatient acute psychiatric ward and a rehabilitation centre

cycle1.result: Minimum dose interval 64.5%; maximum dose 96.7%; ward round reviews 3.2%; discontinuation of unused PRN 0%; review of regularly used PRN 0%; regular vs PRN use documented 33.3%.

cycle2.result: Minimum dose interval 93.5%; maximum dose 100%; ward round reviews 64.5%; discontinuation of unused PRN 22.2%; review of regularly used PRN 28.5%; regular vs PRN use documented 44.4%.

audits.other_findings: Prompted by a serious incident. 100% compliance was sustained for generic naming, routes, BNF limits, indications and rewriting altered prescriptions.
audits.citation: Shashidhar N, Adegboye O. Evaluating PRN Medication Prescribing Practices in Mental Health Services: A Comparative Audit Following a Serious Incident. BJPsych Open. 2025;11(S1):S276-S276. doi:10.1192/bjo.2025.10672.

audits.title: Audit of ‘As Required’ (PRN) Psychotropic Medication Prescriptions in an Adult Inpatient Psychiatric Ward
audits.standard: Trust PRN guidance PHARM-0041-v4.2 (standard 100%): indication, dose/formulation/frequency, minimum interval, maximum 24-hour dose, review date, first-/second-line guidance, review if unused for four weeks
audits.setting: Danby Ward, adult psychiatric inpatient ward, Cross Lane Hospital (Tees, Esk and Wear Valleys NHS Foundation Trust)

cycle1.result: 15 prescriptions with 32 PRN medicines: indication and dosing parameters 32/32 (100%); documented review date 0/32; first-/second-line guidance 0/18 where applicable; review or discontinuation after four weeks unused 0/8.

audits.intervention: Trust-wide post-audit actions: automatic 14-day review date on PRN oral and IM regimens, updated PRN guidance on first-/second-line options with EPMA content and training materials, EPMA upgrade, and EPMA e-learning plus a quick reference handbook.
audits.other_findings: Customisation of regimen dose screens is still in progress. A re-audit is planned after full implementation.
audits.citation: Gupta N, Rodriguez J. Audit of ‘As Required’ (PRN) Psychotropic Medication Prescriptions in an Adult Inpatient Psychiatric Ward. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S297-S297. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11711.

audits.title: Audit of Pro Re Nata (PRN) Medication Use in Acute Mental Health Wards in Luton and Bedfordshire
audits.standard: Guidelines on PRN prescribing and regular review and discontinuation
audits.setting: General adult, old age and CAMHS acute mental health wards, Luton and Bedfordshire (East London NHS Foundation Trust)

cycle1.result: 84% prescribed PRN; 5 of 21 had PRN no longer clinically indicated but still active; PRN protocols not updated after legal status change in 2 patients; oral offered before IM as per guidance.

audits.intervention: Recommended regular PRN review at ward rounds, discontinuing unused PRN, updating protocols after legal status change and MDT review for frequent PRN use.
audits.other_findings: 10 of 21 were prescribed both promethazine and lorazepam; 6 of 21 needed more than 20 PRN doses since admission.
audits.citation: Vijayan K, Purushothaman S. Audit of Pro Re Nata (PRN) Medication Use in Acute Mental Health Wards in Luton and Bedfordshire. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S352-S352. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11752.

audits.title: Pro re nata medication for psychoses: an audit of practice in two metropolitan hospitals.
audits.setting: Two inner city public psychiatry units

cycle1.result: PRN given in 82% of admissions; prescriptions specified a maximum daily dose in 87% but indications in only 6%; administration lacked a reason in 48% and outcome in 64%

audits.other_findings: PRN typical antipsychotics were often co-prescribed with regular atypicals (64%); medication-related morbidity in 37% receiving PRN vs 3% on regular medication only.
audits.citation: Geffen J, Sorensen L, Stokes J, Cameron A, Roberts MS, Geffen L. Pro re nata medication for psychoses: an audit of practice in two metropolitan hospitals. Aust N Z J Psychiatry. 2002;36(5):649-656. doi:10.1046/j.1440-1614.2002.01069.x. PMID: 12225449.

audits.title: Audit: Prescribing PRN medication.
audits.standard: Local trust medicine policy standards for PRN prescribing, based on good clinical practice
audits.setting: Two adolescent wards, St Andrew's Healthcare Hospital

cycle1.result: 36% of PRN medications were not cancelled despite not being used for >1 month; 23% did not have clear indications for use. Most other standards showed full compliance.

audits.other_findings: Recommendations included screening tools (START/STOP) to alert the responsible clinician after a month, making indication an obligatory field, staff awareness and seasonal re-audits.
audits.citation: Adelaide D, Rawther F. Audit: Prescribing PRN medication. Psychiatr Danub. 2017;29(Suppl 3):568-570. PMID: 28953830.

audits.title: As needed or pro re nata medication prescribing accuracy in haematology/oncology: quality improvement initiative.
audits.standard: Reduce PRN prescribing errors from 30% to below 10% over 12 weeks

cycle1.result: 30% PRN prescribing error rate, mainly dose and frequency.

audits.intervention: Four PDSA cycles on tools, education, resources and awareness, including QR-code resources and induction teaching.
audits.citation: Keane N, Deane S, Reilly L, Mannion E, Waldron D, O'Riordan J, et al.. As needed or pro re nata medication prescribing accuracy in haematology/oncology: quality improvement initiative. BMJ Support Palliat Care. 2026. doi:10.1136/spcare-2026-006249. PMID: 42457546.
